Asset type: Matkakirja Athens arrival illustration, year 1873, ONE completely NEW camera-looking opaque landscape image, 1536 x 1024.
Primary request: a NEUTRAL BLACK-AND-WHITE documentary photographic reconstruction of the Acropolis seen northeast from the southwest slope of Philopappou Hill in 1873. Generate the entire new scene from scratch. This is not a conversion, filter, edit or recoloring of a previous image; retain no earlier pixels.
Input images: reference1 is an earlier generated1873 Athens illustration; use ONLY its southwest camera location, overall landmark scale and framing as a loose factual/composition guide. Reference2 is a Getty book page with Dimitrios Constantin's ca1860–1865 southwest Acropolis photograph; use ONLY the factual ruined geometry and Frankish Tower location in its photo, never its printed captions, border or sepia tone. Reference3 is William J. Stillman's Getty1870 Musaeum Hill historical photo; use ONLY period factual topography, tower position and open bare slope. These are factual references, not stylistic image-edit targets. Do not copy source pixels or paper artifacts.
Scene and period: dry rocky Philopappou slope with a naturally worn unpaved route, one sparse irregular olive tree to the left and a few low wild shrubs. The Acropolis dominates the middle distance. Propylaea western gateway is on the LEFT; roofless damaged Parthenon is right of center. Lycabettus hill may appear far right. Small old Athens has scattered low one- and two-storey plaster houses with tiled roofs, mostly to the right below and beyond the rock; no present-day city sprawl. South slopes are largely bare with period masonry ruins and rubble.
CRITICAL archaeological geometry: a tall plain rectangular medieval Frankish Tower stands at the southwest/southern wing of the Propylaea western gateway, at the FAR LEFT END of the Acropolis and far LEFT of the Parthenon, matching the historical photograph references. Simple near-flat top, plain masonry, no elaborate battlements, domes or pointed roof. Temple of Athena Nike is a small temple on the southwest bastion next to/in front of that western gateway cluster in its first rebuilt1835–1836 form. Parthenon is ROOFLESS and visibly broken, with west columns and the long southern colonnade having large missing middle sections and irregular broken entablature, not a continuous restored row; no later marble infills or rebuilt columns. Do not invent intact Classical architecture.
Camera and monochrome: a real camera-looking view, ordinary45mm perspective, subdued natural late-afternoon daylight rendered solely as clean neutral grayscale. ALL tones must be achromatic neutral black, white and gray, with equal red/green/blue component values; ABSOLUTELY NO sepia, brown, warm tint, blue tint, tinted highlights, color, duotone or color wash. Full rich grayscale detail without heavy fake aging, scratches, print borders, HDR or theatrical contrast. Natural optical softness and irregular limestone, bark and vegetation textures; no stamped organic patterns.
Year1873 exclusions: no Zappeion, modern apartments, Acropolis Museum, automobiles, asphalt, electricity wires/poles/lamps, floodlights, antennas, solar panels, cranes, scaffolding, modern rails, concretepaths, modern restorations or modern clothes. No people needed. No text, letters, numbers, signs, logos, watermarks, frame or collage. No museum-artifact replica, painterly rendering or CGI.

assets.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: Matkakirja Paris arrival image number 8, a new BLACK AND WHITE photograph-like reconstruction of Pont Royal and the Tuileries ruins in the year 1873. One image only, 1536x1024 opaque.
Image roles: Image1 is my generated present-day Pont Royal river view, used ONLY to match the left-bank eye-level camera position and five-arch bridge/river framing. Its restored far-right Louvre/Pavillon roof is NOT historical evidence and MUST NOT be retained. Image2 is Pierre Emonts's July1871 public-domain/CC0 Musée Carnavalet photo PH17352: factual source for the burnt Pavillon de Flore and adjacent Tuileries ruin, especially its exposed burnt open roof framework and surviving chimney masonry. Image3 is Carnavalet PH34628 from1883: factual supporting evidence for standing roofless Tuileries walls only; do not copy1883 demolition work or its camera angle. All are visual/factual references, not images to edit. No source pixels, museum photo framing, annotations, paper border, sepia or text reproduced.
Camera and scene: the same general LEFT BANK river position as Image1 looking across the Seine at Pont Royal, eye height about3m above low-quay level, normal40mm lens. Five real modest low stone arches aligned horizontally across the middle of frame, river foreground, diagonal simple stone quay lower right, opposite riverbank and the old Tuileries site behind. Plausible small wood workboat or unmarked nineteenth-century steam launch is enough, no modern boats; no people or faces necessary.
CRITICAL YEAR1873 ROOF CONDITION: behind the opposite-bank trees the standing Tuileries palace wings are an abandoned burnt ruin after the1871 fire, long old masonry walls with black empty window openings, collapsed floors, broken parapets and NO INTACT ROOF. The taller PAVILLON DE FLORE AT THE FAR RIGHT MUST ALSO HAVE A BURNT-DAMAGED ROOF: open skeletal partly collapsed old roof rafters and standing large pale chimney stacks as in Image2, gaps clearly exposing pale sky through the missing roofing. Do NOT draw the smooth intact high slate mansard roof, clean continuous roof slopes, decorative intact ridge, completed restored roof or modern Louvre silhouette from Image1. This is before1874–1876 restoration. The surviving pavilion facade can stand but its roof is distinctly incomplete and wrecked, not restored. The original long central Tuileries ruins remain present in1873; no claim that demolition has already removed them.
Photographic medium: genuinely camera-like mid-nineteenth-century collodion/albumen-photo feel in NEUTRAL BLACK AND WHITE ONLY. All rendered pixels should be black, white, achromatic neutral gray, no brown/sepia/blue/green tint, no coloured foliage or water. Soft restrained contrast, very subtle fine photographic grain and barely perceptible natural lens-edge darkening; not old paper, damage, heavy vignetting or an illustration. Quiet pale natural daylight with believable soft shadows, organic irregular stone, wood and water ripple textures, mild period harbour haze.
Restrictions: no intact restored far-right roof, no1890s/modern urban details, Eiffel Tower, modern museum/glass pyramid, motorboats, modern tourists, automobiles, modern streetlamps, cables, advertising or signs. No visible letters, words, numbers, logos, brands, watermarks, borders, faces, modern protected artwork or named designer objects. Completely new whole-scene generation, no local editing or recolouring of any reference. Retain full1536x1024 landscape.
